crop.notes: Whole article from the 'AT THE OLD STAND' headline and both decks to the closing Joe Elliott quote.

ocr.notes: Accurate; dialect normalized ('knocking' for 'knockin'', 'meeting' for 'meetin''), 'very reticent' shortened to 'reticent', crossheads 'A FOOL IF HE DID' and 'OLD MEN AT THE BUSINESS' run into the text.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Allen was back in St. Louis after six years, denied that Rooke had knocked him out, and planned to challenge any man for the championship, with a bare-knuckle fight in the Indian Nation.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Saturday, December 30, 1882, page 8. article.json has no focus field.

facts.fact: Allen returned to St. Louis the evening before, six years after he left the city
Allen said his reported knockout by George Rooke was a friendly soft-glove set-to in which his foot went through a plank of the stage and he fell
facts.quote: It was a friendly set-to with soft gloves, and before we went at it it was understood we should go light.

facts.fact: Allen said he sparred with Cleary of Philadelphia just after the Rooke meeting and found him not nearly as clever as Rooke
facts.quote: I set to with him just after the meetin' with Rooke, and he isn't nearly as clever as George.

facts.fact: Allen said John L. Sullivan would not fight him
facts.quote: He's a stout young fellow, but bless you, he won't fight. He'd be a fool if he did, for he can make twice the money at knockin' out. I'd meet Sullivan, but he won't meet me. It wouldn't pay him to do so.

facts.fact: Allen came to St. Louis at the invitation of a gentleman who had backed him in nearly all his old fights and intended to set him up in business there

Allen planned to challenge any man in the world for any sum and the championship, hoping to hear from Rooke, Cleary, Mace or Mace's protege; the fight would be held in the Indian Nation on the M., K. & T. road to avoid the police
places: Indian Nation, on the M., K. & T. railroad

facts.fact: In Chicago Allen refused to take part in a hippodrome (fixed fight) with Elliott proposed by 'the Parson' and others, who then spread reports that he was on a spree and a wreck
Allen blamed Joe Elliott of the New York Herald for the story that he was played out
facts.quote: Joe Elliott, the old fellow who writes for the New York Herald, started that story. He's had it in for me for something or other.

notes: The backer is unnamed here; article 100 names John C. Gropper as his reported saloon partner (index fact id 000, so existing_fact left blank). The image prints 'knochin' ont' (a misprint) in Allen's first quote, so only the clean part is quoted.
